Set the **root path** to match your proxy prefix by starting the server with `--root-path`:

```console
$ fastapi run main.py --root-path /api
```

**Why the docs page breaks:** When you open the integrated docs UI (the frontend), it would expect to get the OpenAPI schema at `/openapi.json`[1] instead of the prefixed path. So, the frontend (that runs in the browser) would try to reach `/openapi.json` and wouldn't be able to get the OpenAPI schema.[1]

**How `--root-path` fixes it:** FastAPI uses this `root_path` to create the default `server` in OpenAPI with the URL provided by `root_path`.[5] Your application code doesn't change. The proxy would be "stripping" the path prefix on the fly before transmitting the request to the server, keeping your application convinced that it is being served at `/app`, so that you don't have to update all your code to include the prefix[1].

**Things to check:**
- This setup assumes Nginx strips the `/api` prefix before forwarding requests to FastAPI.
- Open the docs through the proxy, at `/api/docs`. If you try the docs UI served by the server directly, without the path prefix in the URL, it won't work, because it expects to be accessed through the proxy.[5]

The FastAPI docs use Traefik as the example proxy, not Nginx. For the Nginx side of the setup (stripping the prefix), see the Nginx documentation.
